FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 93) (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on recommendation 
of the Methods of Sampling and Test for Petroleum, its Products, Gaseous Fuels and Lubricants Sectional 
Committee and approval of the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


This Indian Standard was first published in 1979 and was adopted from ASTM D-1321-76. 


In this revision method of sample preparation and test procedure are modified. Considerable assistance was 
derived from ASTM D1321-16 “Standard test method for needle penetration of petroleum waxes”. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical 
values ( revised y 


IS 1448 (Part 93) : 2021 


Indian Standard 


METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM 
AND ITS PRODUCTS 


PART 93 DETERMINATION OF NEEDLE PENETRATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard (Part 93) describes a method for the 
empirical estimation of the consistency of waxes 
derived from petroleum by measurement of the extent 
of penetration of a standard needle. This method is 
applicable to waxes having a penetration of not greater 
than 250. 


2 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The sample is heated to at least 17 °C above its 
expected congealing point or melting point, poured 
into a container, further air cooled under controlled 
conditions. The sample is then conditioned at test 
temperature in a water bath. Penetration is measured 
with a penetrometer, which has a standard needle that 
penetrates into the sample for 5 s under a load of 100 g. 


3 SIGNIFICANCE 


Petroleum waxes differ in hardness. Needle penetration 
is a measurement of hardness. Hardness may have a 
significant effect upon other physical properties. 


4 DEFINITION 


4.1 Penetration of Petroleum Wax 


The depth, in tenths ofa millimetre, to which a standard 
needle penetrates into the wax under defined conditions. 


NOTE — As an example, a penetration reading of 85 from the 
indicator scale corresponds to a penetration depth of 8.5 mm. 


5 APPARATUS 


5.1 Penetrometer 


For applying the standard needle to the surface of 
the sample specimen and for measuring the extent 
of penetration at the conclusion of the test. The 
penetrometer shall be constructed in such a manner 
that the accurate placement of the tip of the needle 
at the level surface of the specimen may be made 
while maintaining a ‘zero’ reading on the indicator. 
The apparatus shown in Fig. | represents a composite 
drawing illustrating the two available types of 
instrument, one with an adjustable table and the other 
with an adjustable needle assembly; the use of either 
type instrument is permissible. The loaded needle shall 


fall, when released without appreciable friction. The 
instrument shall be provided with levelling screws 
and a spirit level to maintain the plunger shaft in a true 
vertical position. The indicator scale shall be calibrated 
in tenths of a millimeter divisions having a range of 
at least 250 tenths of millimetres. Alternatively, an 
auto penetrometer may be used complying to the test 
method. 


Fic. 1 PENETROMETER 


5.2 Timing Device 


An automatic timing release mechanism attached to the 
penetrometer may be used. Alternatively, a stop watch 
graduated in 0.1 s intervals may be used. 


5.3 Needle and Plunger 


The needle shall be approximately 83 mm in length 
and conform to the dimensions shown in Fig. 2. It shall 
be symmetrically tapered at one end to a cone whose 
angle shall be within the range from 8 degree 55 min 


IS 1448 (Part 93) : 2021 


to 9 degree 25 min over the entire length of the cone. 
The axis of the cone shall be coincident with the shaft 
axis within 0.125 mm maximum run out (total indicator 
reading). The tapered section of the needle shall be 
made from fully hardened and tempered stainless 
steel, grade 440 C or equal, Rockwell hardness 
C 57 to 60. After tapering, the point shall be ground 
off to a truncated cone, the smaller base of which shall 
be from 0.14 to 0.16 mm in diameter. The truncation 
shall be square with the needle axis within 2 degree 
and the edge shall be sharp and free from burrs. The 
conical surface and the truncation shall be finished to a 
smoothness of 0.2 um. The final mass of the needle shall 
be 2.5 + 0.05 g. The total mass of the plunger shall be 
47.5 + 0.05 g; a mass of 50 + 0.05 g is required for 
mounting on the plunger (see Note). 


NOTE — Penetration needles shall be tested for conformity 
with these permissible variations by a qualified testing agency. 


5.4 Test Specimen Container 


Consisting of a brass cylinder open at both ends, having 
a 25.4 + 1.6 mm inside diameter 31.8 + 1.6 mm height, 
and 3.2 + 1.6 mm wall thickness. To prevent slippage of 
very hard wax, a few screw threads or grooves shall be 
cut into the centre part of the inside wall of the cylinder. 
The cylinder shall be placed on a base plate of brass, 
wetted with an equal volume mixture of glycerine and 
water, when casting a test specimen. 


5.5 Test Room or Cabinet 
Capable of being maintained at 23.9 + 2.2 °C. 


5.6 Water Bath 


Water bath of at least 10 litres capacity capable 
of being maintained at the test temperature within 
+0.1°C (see Note at 7.2). The water bath shall be made 
of glass or have a window to permit a horizontal view 


of the specimen. It shall be possible to immerse the 
test specimen in the bath to a depth of not less than 
102 mm and to support it on a perforated conditioning 
shelf not less than 51 mm from the bottom of the bath. 
The bath also shall be equipped with a rigid perforated 
test shelf about 51 mm below the water level to support 
the specimen during the penetration by the needle. 


5.7 Thermometer 


Total immersion type conforming to the following 
specification: 


Range 25 to 55 °C 
Graduation 0.1 *C 
Longer lines at each 0.5 °C 
Figured at each LC 

Scale error not to exceed 0.1 °C 
Expansion chamber to 105 °C 
allow heating to 

Overall length 379 +5 mm 
Stem diameter 7 to 8 mm 
Bulb length 25 to 35 mm 
Bulb diameter 6 to7 mm 


Distance from bottom of 115 to 135 mm 
bulb to line at 25 °C 
Distance from bottom of 
bulb to line at 55 °C 


Ice point range 


324 to 344 mm 


—0.5 to + 0.5 percent 


Distance from bottom of 60 to 70 mm 
bulb to ice point 

Distance to bottom of 80 mm (Min) 
contraction Chamber 

Distance to top of 100 mm (Max) 


contraction chamber 


Shaft drilled out and length adjusted to give final mass of 2.5 + 0.05 


g 


All dimensions in millimetres 


Fic. 2 NEEDLE FOR PENETRATION TEST 


5.8 Brass Plate 


63.5 + 1.6 x 39 + 1.6 x 6.4 + 1.6 mm for supporting 
test specimen during preparation of the sample. The 
specimen support is placed on corks during the cooling 
period. 


6 PREPARATION OF TEST SPECIMEN 


Heat the wax sample to approximately 20 °C above its 
congealing point using care to prevent local overheating. 
Stir until the sample is homogeneous and free from 
air bubbles. In the test room or cabinet maintained at 
25 + 2 °C, place the brass plate on two corks, and wet 
the upper surface of the plate with a mixture of equal 
volumes of glycerin and water. Place the test specimen 
container on the plate and then pour the melted wax 
into it in such a way that a convex meniscus is formed. 
Allow the container and contents to cool in the room at 
25 +2 °C for 1 h. Then shave any excess wax from the 
top of the container and remove the brass plate. Place 
the smooth wax surface up. Condition the specimen in 
the bath at the test temperature within + 0.1 °C for Ih 
(see Note). 

NOTE — Very hard waxes occasionally will shrink away from 

the walls of the test specimen container; in such cases, it is 

permissible to wedge the specimen in the container. 


7 PROCEDURE 


7.1 Reverse the penetrometer base and place the 
penetrometer head over the edge of the water bath and 
above the perforated test shelf used for supporting the 
specimen. It may be necessary to place a weight on the 
base of the penetrometer to counterbalance the head 
(see Note). Level the penetrometer and the perforated 
shelf in the water bath. 


NOTE — Alternatively, the penetrometer may be placed 
in the water bath. Likewise a small bath may be placed 
on the penetrometer stand provided the test temperature 
(within + 0.1 °C) and the required water circulation above and 
below the test specimen are maintained and provided further 
that the temperature of the small bath is measured immediately 
before testing each specimen using the thermometer specified 
in 5.7. Emergent stem corrections shall be applied when 
the correction equals or exceeds 0.05 °C. One of the above 
alternatives will be required if the penetrometer is the 
adjustable table type. 


7.2 Place the specimen container on the perforated test 
shelf with the smooth wax surface that had contacted 
the brass plate at the top. Make certain that the test shelf 
cannot teeter during testing. Adjust the water level such 
that it is at least 25 mm above the top surface of the 
specimen and maintain it at the test temperature. 

NOTE — The test may be performed at any temperature in the 

range from 25 to 55 °C. Temperatures 25 °C, 35 °C, 45 °C or 

50 °C normally are used. 


7.3 Place a 50 g weight above the penetrometer needle, 
making a total load of 100 + 0.15 g for the needle and 
all the attachments. Observe that the release mechanism 
does not drag on the shaft and the indicator on the scale 


IS 1448 (Part 93) : 2021 


is in the “zero” position. Adjust either the indicator 
assembly or the table depending upon the type of 
instrument, until the tip of the needle nearly touches 
the surface of the specimen. Securely lock the movable 
assembly in this position. 


7.4 Then, slowly adjust and bring the needle tip to just 
touch the surface of the specimen. Watch the reflection 
of the needle tip for accurate setting. Ensure the bath 
temperature is within the limits. Release the needle 
shaft and hold it free for 5.0 + 0.1 s, by timing this 
interval automatically or with a stop watch graduated 
to 0.1 s. Then gently depress the indicator shaft until it is 
stopped by the needle shaft. Read the penetration from 
the indicator scale. 


7.5 Make four tests at points about equally spaced (not 
less than 12.7 mm apart) on a circumference of atleast 
3.2 mm from the side of the container. Before each 
test, wipe the needle carefully towards its point with a 
clean dry cloth to remove all adhering wax. Position the 
needle as described in 7.4, and proceed with the test. 


8 REPORT 


Record as a single test value the average scale reading 
for the four penetrations on the prepared specimen and 
report to the nearest 0.1 mm. Also report the actual test 
temperature used. 


9 PRECISION 


9.1 Repeatability 


The difference between successive results obtained 
by the same operator with the same apparatus under 
constant operating conditions on identical test material 
would, in the long run, in the normal and correct 
operation of the test method, exceed the following 
values in only one case in twenty. 


At 25 °C repeatability = 1.72 [10 000920] 
At 40 °C repeatability = 0.09905 (#)!!75 
where 


X = penetration. 


9.2 Reproducibility 


The difference between two single and independent 
results obtained by different operators working in 
different laboratories on identical test material would, 
in the long run, exceed the following values in only one 
case in twenty. 


At 25 °C reproducibility = 4.81 [10 00020] 

At 40 °C Reproducibility = 0.1746 (x) 1175 
where 

X = penetration. 


9.3 The repeatability and reproducibility, calculated 
from the above equations for selected penetration 
values are shown in Table 1.
